title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #287: Unit Fraction Decomposition Gaps. Status: OPEN

title: Isunitfractiondecomp
content: An Egyptian fraction representation of 1: a sorted list of distinct integers > 1 whose reciprocals sum to 1. ns.length ≥ 2 ∧ ns.Sorted (· < ·) ∧ (∀ n ∈ ns, n > 1) ∧ (ns.map (fun n => (1 : ℚ) / n)).sum = 1

title: Maxgap
content: (ns.zip ns.tail).foldl (fun acc p => max acc (p.2 - p.1)) 0

title: No Consecutive Reciprocals
content: **Erdős's Theorem**: The maximum gap is at least 2.  Equivalently: 1 is not the sum of reciprocals of consecutive integers n, n+1, ..., n+k for any n, k. ∀ ns : List ℕ, IsUnitFractionDecomp ns → maxGap ns ≥ 2

title: Erdos 287 Conjecture
content: **Erdős's Conjecture (OPEN)**: The maximum gap is at least 3.  If true, the example [2, 3, 6] would be optimal (max gap = 3). ∀ ns : List ℕ, IsUnitFractionDecomp ns → maxGap ns ≥ 3

title: Erdos 287
content: Known: max gap ≥ 2 (Erdős). Conjectured: max gap ≥ 3. Best known example: [2, 3, 6] with gap 3. ∀ ns : List ℕ, IsUnitFractionDecomp ns → maxGap ns ≥ 2 := no_consecutive_reciprocals
